0.long_answer: Reactive thrombocythemia is a condition in which there is an increased production of platelets in response to another underlying condition, such as inflammation or tissue damage. In the context of diabetes, particularly when hyperglycemia is uncontrolled, platelets become more reactive, which increases the risk of thrombotic complications. These thrombotic events include conditions such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Thus, the condition associated with reactive thrombocythemia that is also seen in diabetes is the predisposition to thrombotic complications.
